stories.completed: Done. You reached the final study summary screen.

items.title: Create medical flashcards
items.description: Create a deck, add two basic cards and study them through to the summary.
steps: Tap “Add deck” and create a new set.
Add the first basic card and tap “Next”.
Add the second card and tap “Save” to return to the deck.
Tap “Study” in the top-right corner of the deck.
Go through the cards until the summary screen.

items.title: Turn pharmacology notes into cloze cards
items.description: Create a deck, add one cloze card and finish a short study session.
steps: Tap “Add deck” and create a new set.
Select part of the text, use cloze and tap “Save”.
Tap “Study” in the top-right corner of the deck.
Go through study until the summary screen.

items.title: Review before a colloquium
items.description: Start studying from an example deck and reach the repeat-or-exit choice.
steps: Tap “Study” on one of the example decks.
Rate each card as “I know” or “I don't know”.
On the final screen, choose repeat or return to the deck.

proof.heading: What medical students want from a flashcard tool
proof.footer: In conversations with medical students, the same frustrations kept coming up: creating flashcards takes too long, images are awkward to work with, reviews feel cumbersome and offline learning isn't reliable. Fishki is built to solve exactly those problems.

quotes.name: Hannah
quotes.quote: I want reviews like in Anki, but with simpler syncing between my tablet, phone and offline mode.

quotes.name: Kate
quotes.quote: The best option would combine Anki and Quizlet: quick review and regular spaced repetition.

quotes.name: Adam
quotes.quote: I would like more control: changing intervals, shuffling flashcards and easily swapping the question and answer.
